deck_title: Clairaut r(s)*sin(psi) surface-of-revolution geodesic invariant vs naive constant-angle rhumb loxodrome rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Alexis Claude Clairaut (1733) & Emmy Noether (1918) surface-of-revolution geodesic angular-momentum conservation law (conserving C_Clairaut = r(s) * sin(psi(s)) = r_0 * sin(psi_0) across expanding parallel circles r(u) = r_0 * (1 + u) so sin(psi) = sin(psi_0)/(1+u) and geodesic curvature kappa_g = 0, locking C_active / C_Clairaut = 1.0000x across all 17 stations u in [0.000, 1.000] with 0/17 violated) versus naive constant-angle rhumb-line / loxodrome wrapping (sin(psi) = sin(psi_0), which inflates r*sin(psi) by 1 + u to 1.2500x at S4, 1.5000x at S8, and 2.0000x at S16 across 16/17 stations) and 64-step Christoffel geodesic curvature quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Procedural vine/ivy wrapping around vases and columns, tensioned leather straps on armor/barrels, composite filament winding, and geodesic ribbon trails on surfaces of revolution
Enforcing Clairaut relation sin(psi(r)) = C / r so wrapped straps have zero geodesic curvature (kappa_g = 0) and never slip sideways under tension
Predicting exact turnaround parallel radius r_min = C where sin(psi) = 1 (90-degree equator bounce)
not_for: Uniform right circular cylinders where r(z) === r_0 everywhere and helices coincide with loxodromes
